decision: How do we tell parents about the kids' rewards program without a new home page section, and what should the /rewards page look like?
primary_axis: where rewards sit in the 'What you get each month' grid; how the /rewards page leads (explain, shop, path, letter, calculator)
where: Live prototype. Grid: /?variant=now|C|E|C2|C3|E2|CE (src/components/rewards-card-prototype.tsx). Page: /rewards?variant=A|B|C|D|E (src/components/rewards-prototype.tsx). Branch site/rewards-prototype.
invariants: points come from checked page scans (finished work), never from scores or from a book arriving
shared facts in src/components/rewards-data.tsx; every number (10 a page, 25 a full week, 50 a book, prize prices) is a placeholder for Savar
real prize examples (iPad, zoo, aquarium, movie tickets, gift card, toys) are approved by Savar (2026-10-09)

grid.bet: Seventh card under the photo, same kind as the others, soft orange
grid.benefit: Quietest; reads as part of the offer

grid.bet: Prize tile replaces the photo: gradient tile, 3-prize ladder, button
grid.benefit: Most visible; shows the iPad on the home page
grid.risk: Loses the only photo in the section

grid.bet: One linked sentence inside 'Instant answer check'
grid.benefit: Zero new layout; the original 'clickable sentence' idea
grid.risk: Most parents will not see it

grid.bet: Full-width strip under the grid: +10 a page, prize chips, link
grid.benefit: Visible without touching the six cards
grid.risk: Reads like a small new section

grid.bet: A '+10 points a page' sticker on the photo and a caption link

page.bet: Explainer: earn, prizes table with time to reach, how a prize gets home, FAQ
page.benefit: Answers every parent question in order

page.bet: Prize shop: big prize tiles with a points filter; earning shrinks to chips
page.benefit: Most fun to browse; a child can look at it
page.risk: Feels like a store, not a learning product

page.bet: Points path: monthly sum, then a timeline from day 1 to the iPad
page.benefit: Makes 'saving up' concrete and shows the first prize is close
page.risk: Shows the iPad is 2.5 years away

page.bet: Letter to parents: why we reward finished work, a table, a plain prize list
Calculator: plan and days a week change the points and time to each prize
page.benefit: Interactive; parent sees their own case
page.risk: Exposes the economics; more to maintain

round_2.feedback: Savar liked grid C and E. The message is: your child earns rewards as they finish their workbooks and build a daily habit. The grid must answer the parent's doubt: how do you get my child to actually do the work?
round_2.finding: Phones hide the grid photo (warm.css, D-072), so E and E2 show nothing about rewards on a phone. Only a card-based version reaches phone visitors.

options.bet: 'Daily practice' becomes 'Daily practice, rewarded': rewards for every finished page and every week of the habit, plus a link
options.benefit: Reward sits next to the habit it builds; works on phones

options.bet: The card asks the parent's question: 'How do we keep them going?' Answer: rewards. Soft orange card
options.benefit: Names the doubt out loud; easiest to find
options.risk: A question title breaks the pattern of the other cards

options.bet: Sticker on the photo links to /rewards; caption carries the habit message
C2's card plus the sticker on the photo, both link to /rewards
options.benefit: Card carries the message everywhere; sticker adds a visual hook on desktop
options.risk: Two links to the same page

chosen.page: D (letter to parents, eyebrow 'Rewards for kids')
chosen.polish: 'See the rewards' link: one continuous underline under the text and the arrow
